column1: First-pass hypotheses from the project strategy and supplied SMARTfit materials. Validate with real sales conversations and buyers.

column2: Clinic owner/director; PT/OT/SLP lead; neuro-rehab manager; procurement
column3: Clinical fit, patient/staff workflow, setup, space, evidence, assessment capabilities, budget/procurement.
column4: What does this system do? Which model/configuration fits our space and workflow? What evidence applies to our population?
column6: Clinical efficacy, diagnosis, treatment, reimbursement/CPT, patient outcomes
column7: Start with supported use/feature language; clinician review needed for clinical content.

column2: Executive director; wellness/activity director; clinical leader; operator
column3: Resident engagement, accessibility, group logistics, staff capacity, space, funding/business case.
column4: What could a program look like for residents with different mobility levels? What does the system actually measure?
column6: Fall reduction, dementia prevention, cognitive decline, care-cost savings
column7: Don't present program concepts as proven health outcomes.

column2: Performance director; athletic trainer; coach; sports-science lead
column3: Training goals, team throughput, facility fit, progression, comparison with alternatives.
column4: How are systems configured for individual and team training? What evidence supports transfer to sport?
column6: Faster reaction, game performance, injury prevention, return-to-play guarantees
column7: Separate training features from measured competition outcomes.

column2: District administrator; principal; PE/adaptive PE leader; after-school program
column3: Group size, supervision, schedule, space, accessibility, procurement, privacy.
column4: How does the equipment fit a gym or multipurpose room? What setup and supervision are needed?
column6: Academic improvement, impulse-control outcomes, sensory/developmental claims
column7: Review child privacy/safety and distinguish general exergaming research.

column2: Training director; procurement; occupational health; program lead
column3: Operational setting, durability/configuration, procurement route, training, data/security.
column4: What configurations support the planned training? What procurement or territory limits apply?
column6: Readiness, TBI, resilience, cognitive performance or government procurement promises
column7: Confirm market permissions and public-sector procurement facts.

column2: Fitness director; community-program manager; YMCA/club leader; operator
column3: Program design, user groups, engagement, room/space, staffing, business planning.
column4: How could brain-body activities fit our existing wellness program? What equipment and license are involved?
column6: Medical prevention/treatment, dementia mitigation, ROI guarantees
column7: Use wellness framing and source all product details.

column2: PI; lab director; faculty; clinical researcher; equipment buyer
column3: Technical detail, protocol fit, data exports, research status, institutional terms.
column4: What features are documented? What research has actually tested the product?
column6: Partnership, endorsement, validation, diagnostic or regulatory claims
column7: Avoid implying relationships; use primary papers and current technical documents.
